The earlier deliverance supplies a pattern for explaining the saving power of Christ’s blood. His mention of the sign of the Cross belongs to the argument he makes within this catechetical text.

readings.title: Why the suffering must be real

paragraphs.text: Cyril argues that an apparent death would make redemption itself merely apparent. He therefore insists on the reality of Christ’s crucifixion and connects its confession with the Resurrection that follows. His references to Golgotha identify the setting from which he addresses his hearers.

overview.text: Cyril explains Christ’s resurrection through the scriptural testimony cited by the apostles. readings.title: Why Cyril returns to Scripture

paragraphs.text: Cyril takes the apostolic phrase about resurrection according to the Scriptures as a reason to examine earlier testimony. readings.title: How Clement relates faith and obedience

paragraphs.text: Clement connects Abraham’s departure from home with his confidence in God’s promised blessing.
